units_note: Drawing units, frame-relative. 5 units = spacing between bus bars. Page and title block measured from ES-011511; page parts measured from Sammy's restyled ES_01 (GND_Section_Devider_REFERENCE).

text.line_spacing_note: Multi-line text (e.g. a termination block's TERMINATION attribute): each extra line adds height x line_spacing_factor. 1.667 is AutoCAD's single line spacing for MText.

group_mounted.note: Measured from NTT-013627 / PRIME-014034 / ES_12. A part too tall for the page is split: column 1 is cut after the last level that fits and the rest continue in a column beside it (FIXED_011511 ES_12, CORRECTED_FIXED_011511 ES_11). column_pitch is A phase to A phase; it is widened if the breakers of neighbouring columns would come closer than column_clearance. continuation_start_gap is from the main bus's nearest phase to where a continuation column starts.

placeholder_sizes.note: PLACEHOLDERS until the real blocks are catalogued. Widths include labels. A single-breaker feeder is drawn like a main breaker, so it uses the same height. group_mounted_width is only used when the feeder block isn't catalogued.

main_bus.note: Bus height positions are the B (middle) phase. content_bottom_y = ground bus (20.94) + 10 clearance.
main_bus.page_break_note: Bus runs past the last divider at a page break (min..max), plus room for the break block's to/from label (placeholder until the block exists).

main_breaker.note: Gaps measured from NTC-013632 / NTT-013628 (breaker 15 from the bus, input about 30 beyond the breaker).
main_breaker.u_turn_note: U-turns for main and single breakers (2026-10-13). When the termination is fed from the other side than the breaker, the bus leaves the breaker, turns, runs u_turn_width to the right and comes back u_turn_termination_rise, where the termination block sits. The turn is just far enough that the termination's text stays u_turn_text_clearance clear of the breaker and its text (sizes from catalog/blocks.json). u_turn_depth is used for the U-turns of a breaker fed on the bus side.

wire_labels.note: A label on every wire the program draws (decision 2026-11-09), from the wire label legend of the hybrid NTT-013628: the prefix for the wire's layer, then a number with 'digits' digits (4A001). Numbers for now: voltage tap n's wires from the 3-line to its fuse are 2n-1, from its fuse to what it feeds 2n (one tap: 4A001 / 4A002, as in the hybrid); the three phases share the number. Placed centred on the wire's longest straight run, 'gap' above it (or beside it, turned, on an upright wire). Wires on layers not listed here are not labelled. The labels go on layer 0 (Sammy, 2026-11-10).

page_title.note: The title at the bottom right of every page, its right end at x (just left of the title block), its middle at y; measured from the hybrid NTT-013628 (2026-11-09). mtext_format is the AutoCAD MText formatting from that drawing (bold Century Gothic, spaced out, underlined); {title} is where the words go.

interlocks.note: Dashed line between two interlocked main breakers (decision 2026-10-26), as in Sabey-011486 and NTT-013631 but on its own layer (Sammy added INTERLOCK to HYPER_A, 2026-10-26), at the breakers' mid-height, from start_past_left_c right of the left main's C terminal (through its label, as the references do) to end_before_right_a short of the right main's A terminal. Mains at different heights: the line steps halfway between the divider and the right section's contents. The text is centred on the line after the left main's block, one list entry per line of text, with a background mask so the dashes don't run through it.

input_output.note: Sammy's input/output block. Not flipped = from/to the bottom; flipped = from/to the top.

bus_break.note: Where a bus is cut (page break, or a too-tall column): 3P_TIDE_R0 sits on the A-phase end (CONN_A), BRACKET_TEXT_R0 stands just past the end, centred on B, with the to/from label. Gap measured from CORRECTED_FIXED_011511 ES_11.
bus_break.tilde_flip_note: Where the bus arrives on a page, the tilde is mirrored with only this flip setting, so its A/B/C letters sit on the incoming side (tested on the block 2026-10-13: Flip state1 mirrors left-right; Flip state2 is for the vertical state).
bus_break.flip_note_vertical: Tested on the blocks 2026-10-22: on both the tilde and the bracket, Flip state1 mirrors left-right (horizontal bus) and Flip state2 up-down (vertical bus). Only the one named here is turned on. A vertical bus cut (or continued) with its bracket BELOW the end, e.g. the bottom of a column below the main bus, is flipped up-down (Sammy, 2026-10-22).
bus_break.bracket_stretch_note: Beside a block's pins (a meter's CT inputs, or its voltage FROM another section) the bracket is stretched so its grip lines up with the outer wire (Sammy, 2026-11-17, after doing it by hand). Read from the block 2026-11-17: in its VERTICAL BRACKET state Distance1 is 10 as drawn, its grip then 5 below the middle; each unit more moves the grip and both arms one unit out. So 3 wires 5 apart keep 10; 6 CT wires (25 apart top to bottom) get 17.5. Other brackets are left as drawn.
bus_break.column_label_note: Too-tall split (2026-10-13): the bracket where a column is cut says column_cut_label; the bracket where the next column starts says where the bus comes from (the part below the main bus / above it).

feeder.note: Group-mounted feeder breaker (Sammy's block). Drawn as a LEFT-side breaker; the right-side one is the same block with only `mirror_parameter` turned on (the mirror that goes with `visibility`: MIRROR-3W for 3 PHASE-3 WIRE). The block mirrors about the vertical bus's B phase, as in ES_12. Taps run from each vertical-bus phase to the breaker; the nearest phase's tap is `tap_length` long.
feeder.provision_note: A provision is tapped out like a breaker (taps end where the breaker would connect); its note starts provision_text_gap beyond the tap ends, centred on B. First line is provision_heading (or provision_heading_without_info when the engineer left the info empty), then the engineer's line. From IMS-REFERENCE.
feeder.space_note: A SPACE slot (an unused position, decision 2026-10-19) is drawn like a provision (solid taps out to where a breaker would connect) with just this text, in the same place as a provision's note.

current_transformers.note: CT set block (Sammy's 3_CTS_3L_R1, decision 2026-10-21). On a vertical run (a riser, a tie's run, the base of a group-mounted bus) the CT LEFT states are used, markers CONN_A_L / B_L / C_L; polarity always points toward the source. The program places the set wherever it fits, keeping `clearance` from the bus and the breaker, and fills the CT numbers, shorting-kit number and the meter it goes to.

voltage_taps.note: Voltage tap block (Sammy's 3P_Voltage_Tap, decision 2026-10-22). On a vertical run (a main's incoming feed, between the breaker and the termination) the vertical_state is used, its vertical_markers (A, B, C) on the phases; the wires leave to the right to 'TO FA-n SHEET #'. Each tap keeps `clearance` from the breaker, the next tap and the termination; the run grows to fit. The program fills in the fuse number; the sheet keeps its default until device pages exist.

line_side_breakers.note: A line-side (load-bank) breaker tied into a main breaker's feed in the next section (decision 2026-10-22), measured from Sabey-011475 (52-LBBA into 52-MA-GEN-A). The tie leaves the main's line side nearest the breaker: tie_gap from the main breaker's line-side terminals to the tie's nearest phase (A on top of the tie, staggered, a dot where each phase tees into the riser). The line-side breaker's line-side terminals are gap_to_breaker beyond the tie's outer phase; its output termination gap_breaker_to_output beyond its other end.

device_pages.note: Device pages after the 3-line pages: one page per section (decision 2026-11-09, as in the hybrid NTT-013628), its devices placed left to right in rows from the top left (unit_gap apart side by side, row_gap between rows), clear of the title block; a section that doesn't fit carries on on another page. Devices in the same section are wired; anything leaving the section, and anything from the 3-line, gets a TO / FROM bracket (the bus-break bracket block).
device_pages.sheets_before_pages_note: SHEET numbers on the drawing are the drawing's overall sheet numbers (decision 2026-11-10): the pages kept before the 3-line (TOC, legend, BOM: keep_layouts in autocad_settings.json) come first, so ES_01 is sheet 4. Must equal the number of keep_layouts; Generate warns if not.
device_pages.boxes_until_blocks_note: PLACEHOLDERS until their blocks exist (Sammy, 2026-11-11 / 2026-11-16): the Ethernet switch (in the section ticked for it), each 3WA's trip unit, each COM800 and each breaker's comms module (labelled with the breaker and the module) are boxes on the device pages, on the non-printing placeholder layer. Shaped like the blocks to come (Sammy, 2026-11-17): the trip unit and the Ethernet switch are tall and skinny like the meter. The ones that take 24 V (trip units, Ethernet switch, COM800s) get + and - on their left edge, + box_plus_pin_from_top below the top and - box_minus_pin_from_bottom above the bottom (Sammy, 2026-11-17: + at the top, - at the bottom of every device). A 3WA's COM190 is part of its trip unit's block (Sammy, 2026-11-17), so when the trip unit is drawn its module is named inside its box and gets no box of its own. The other comms modules (a 3VA's COM060) are small boxes next to the COM800 they connect to, no wires (the Siemens cable powers them).
device_pages.ladder_note: The 24 V ladder, first on each section's page (Sammy, 2026-11-17; src/layout/power_ladder.py). The devices stand in one row, tops lined up, in row_order left to right (lineup order within a kind; a 3VA's COM060s next to their COM800), device_gap before each (its + lane and - lane stand in it, lane_spacing apart). The + wires run along the top, the lowest ladder_zone_gap above the devices' tops, wire_spacing apart, the farther a wire goes the higher; the - wires the same along the bottom, the farther the lower. Each device's + comes down in the gap on its left, its - comes up. Terminal blocks: the + group at the top, its wire in from below; the - group at the bottom, its wire in from above; terminal_pitch apart within a strip. Right of the power supply's section the incoming split stands at the left edge, centred on the row; left of it, at the right. In the power supply's section (Sammy, 2026-11-20): the supply, its fuses fuse_column_gap right of it, fuse_pitch apart, bridged on their line side, moved up beside the + wires as far as no fuse's wire turns down (the first runs straight across along the top) and ladder_zone_gap under any + wire passing over them; the supply's - drops between them, runs a lane under the lowest fuse and comes to the - terminal group in a slot of its own right of the + slots (from above, or from below when the fuses reach lower); the ground strip stands ladder_zone_gap under the supply, its blocks turned (ground.strip_rotation in devices.json), each device's ground wire straight down to an upright tilde. A section wider than a page carries on on its next page: one bracket spanning every wire that carries on. Each wire ends feed_into_box inside a box. Until the fuse block has its markers, each fuse is a box fuse_box_width x fuse_box_height.
device_pages.shipping_split_cable_note: On the shipping splits page at the end (Sammy, 2026-11-11): each split's two females side by side, this far apart pin to pin, a labelled wire between them for each pin used.
device_pages.split_stub_length_note: On the section pages, a male's pin carrying a wire that isn't 24 V (a fuse's phases on their way to a meter or power supply in another section, Sammy 2026-11-11) and isn't wired straight to something on the page gets a labelled stub this long (12, like the Ethernet and ground stubs, so its number and the tilde's text don't run together, 2026-11-20), ending in a tilde that says where the wire goes on (Sammy, 2026-11-19: every tilde says where its wire goes, and the other end says so too). Passing through a section with devices in the way: TO the split it leaves by on one end, FROM the split it came in by on the other. A fuse's phases are wired straight into the split when the fuse lies beside it, and straight into the meter they feed when it stands in the row and they come in on its left.
device_pages.wire_break_note: A tilde on the end of every wire that goes to or comes from a fuse through a TO / FROM bracket (Sammy, 2026-10-23): one TILDE_R0 per wire, its CONN point on the wire end, in its VERTICAL state (the wires stand up), text empty.
device_pages.wire_break_flip_horizontal_note: Lying tildes (wires arriving from the left, beside a power supply) are mirrored with only this flip setting (Sammy, 2026-11-05; Flip state1 mirrors TILDE_R0 left-right, read from the block).
device_pages.wire_break_vertical_text_note: An upright tilde's text (TEXT_V, multi-line) reads upward along its wire, past the tilde. Flip state2 mirrors TILDE_R0 up-down, so a wire arriving from above (the ground strip's stubs, Sammy 2026-11-20) has its text under the tilde (checked in AutoCAD 2026-11-23).
device_pages.wire_break_text_note: A tilde's text (Sammy, 2026-11-20): one line when it is no longer than wire_break_text_one_line characters; otherwise two lines, broken at the space that makes the longer line shortest. Never three: if that line is still long, the label is just wider. It stays on one line where the wires beside it are closer together than two lines need (two lines' height plus the clearance; a terminal strip's stubs, 2.5 apart), and while the block's attribute isn't multi-line. The layout keeps room for the text so it can't run into its neighbours: its width is estimated as characters x character_width (measured in AutoCAD 2026-11-20: 0.89 to 1.13 per character at height 1.25, so 1.15 is on the safe side); its height is text height + line spacing per extra line. The text starts offset past the tilde (before it when mirrored), centred on the wire, as TILDE_R0 draws it.
device_pages.from_fuse_label_note: A power supply's inputs when its fuse is in another section (decision 2026-11-05). to_meter_label is used for a fuse going TO a power supply too.
device_pages.remote_display_note: A meter's remote display stands to the left of the meter: the USB line runs remote_display_gap left from the meter's USB marker, then up remote_display_rise into the display's USB marker (at its bottom).
